canonicalRecord.finding_label: Upstream donor routes regenerate methionine for SAMe synthesis
canonicalRecord.finding_summary: Folate-dependent methionine synthase and betaine-dependent BHMT regenerate methionine from homocysteine. Choline can supply betaine. MAT then uses methionine and ATP to form SAMe.
canonicalRecord.finding_interpretation: This establishes connected precursor provision. It does not make folate, betaine or choline MAT reactants, demonstrate that more intake raises synthesis, or resolve a donor-inadequacy constraint on MAT capacity.
canonicalRecord.finding_statement: Folate and betaine remethylation regenerate methionine upstream of MAT-dependent SAMe formation; choline can contribute through betaine.
canonicalRecord.synthesis: Existing reviewed PM1-F1, PM2-F1/PM2-F2 and PM3-F1 establish the successive reaction identities. Folate provides 5-methyltetrahydrofolate for B12-dependent methionine synthase, while betaine supplies the alternative BHMT reaction, predominantly in liver and kidney. Choline oxidation can supply betaine. The regenerated methionine is available to the MAT reaction. Evidence supports the route, without requiring each donor to act directly on MAT.
canonicalRecord.synthesis_limitations: Tissue expression, alternative methionine supply and pathway compensation limit generalisation. SAMe and SAM:SAH are pool-state measurements rather than isolated synthesis rates. No established limiting effect on MAT capacity or nutrient-replete intake benefit is claimed.

canonicalRecord.finding_label: Upstream donor routes regenerate methionine for SAMe synthesis
canonicalRecord.finding_summary: Folate-dependent methionine synthase and betaine-dependent BHMT regenerate methionine from homocysteine. Choline can supply betaine. MAT then uses methionine and ATP to form SAMe.
canonicalRecord.finding_interpretation: This establishes connected precursor provision. It does not make folate, betaine or choline MAT reactants, demonstrate that more intake raises synthesis, or resolve a donor-inadequacy constraint on MAT capacity.
canonicalRecord.finding_statement: Folate and betaine remethylation regenerate methionine upstream of MAT-dependent SAMe formation; choline can contribute through betaine.
canonicalRecord.synthesis: Existing reviewed PM1-F1, PM2-F1/PM2-F2 and PM3-F1 establish the successive reaction identities. Folate provides 5-methyltetrahydrofolate for B12-dependent methionine synthase, while betaine supplies the alternative BHMT reaction, predominantly in liver and kidney. Choline oxidation can supply betaine. The regenerated methionine is available to the MAT reaction. Evidence supports the route, without requiring each donor to act directly on MAT.
canonicalRecord.synthesis_limitations: Tissue expression, alternative methionine supply and pathway compensation limit generalisation. SAMe and SAM:SAH are pool-state measurements rather than isolated synthesis rates. No established limiting effect on MAT capacity or nutrient-replete intake benefit is claimed.

record.title: MAT2B and MAT2A stability — proposed Finding
record.proposition: MAT2B association can preserve MAT2A protein or catalytic stability in purified-human-enzyme and mammalian-cell experiments. This supports a stability contribution to enzyme regulation, not an exclusive explanation of MAT2B action or a demonstrated increase in human SAMe synthesis flux.
record.capRationale: No existing cap triggered by Directness 2, Bias Protection 1, Precision 1 and Replication 1. Raw and adjusted 5/8. No extra decrement for model boundaries.
record.scopeNote: Preview-only proposed synthesis of an experimental component already present in F1's supporting evidence, with independently recovered cellular corroboration. Not a canonical Finding or dietary lever. Activity preservation and protein stability are related but non-identical endpoints.

rationale.D: Both experiments directly test the explicitly model-bounded stability proposition. No bridge to human brain flux or nutritional response is included; those propositions are excluded rather than silently scored.
rationale.B: Orthogonal activity readouts, protein identity/binding assays, cell depletion/knockout and wild-type/mutant rescue offer meaningful protection. Representative blots, limited independently quantified preparation counts and incompletely reported masking retain Bias Protection 1; these are not proof of a critical flaw.
rationale.P: Activity-decay time courses and protein-chase contrasts support a stability contribution. Cellular results are largely representative repeated blots, with no harmonised stability effect interval across models. Precision 1 concerns magnitude and boundary uncertainty, not an invented sample-size threshold.
rationale.R: The Bailey and 2024 cell-study author groups are separate; both support a stability contribution using different models/endpoints. This is partial independent corroboration, not two exact-endpoint replications. Replication 1, not 2. Independent replication was not established in this assessment. This qualification concerns an identical model and stability endpoint, not the verified partial corroboration.

limitations: Partial cross-model corroboration does not quantify MAT2B-dependent stability or SAMe flux in the human brain.
Does not establish that stability is the only MAT2B mechanism: allosteric/catalytic interpretations remain relevant.
No dietary methionine, folate, betaine, choline or ADHD intervention effect was assessed.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: No experiment falsifying the scoped stability contribution was verified. Alternative catalytic/allosteric mechanisms challenge an exclusive stability-only claim, which is explicitly not the assessed proposition.

targetedChecks.access: Scite full text; enzyme-assay Methods, inhibition, binding and stability Results appraised
targetedChecks.assessment: Purified human MAT2A lost activity during substrate-free incubation at 37 C; MAT2B preserved activity. Coupled phosphate and direct LC-MS assays distinguish stability from steady-state kinetic effects. Activity half-life about 2.3 minutes without MAT2B; activity retained over the 120-minute experiment with MAT2B. Technical repeats do not constitute independent replication.

targetedChecks.role: Independent partial corroboration of protein stability
targetedChecks.access: Scite full text; cell perturbation/rescue Results and cycloheximide-chase Methods appraised
targetedChecks.assessment: Separate research group: depletion, knockout and wild-type versus binding-domain-mutant rescue support MAT2B-dependent MAT2A protein stability in mammalian cell models. Protein abundance/chase differs from purified-enzyme activity decay. Mostly representative blots with two or three repeats; no pooled half-life or universal flux effect is claimed. Later tumour/diet experiments do not establish a nutritional PM recommendation.

targetedChecks.role: Contextual structural/allosteric interpretation; challenges stability-only explanations
targetedChecks.access: Scite full-text conformational Results, Discussion and construct Methods appraised
targetedChecks.assessment: CryoEM conformers suggest additional allosteric regulation. Catalytic-activity arguments partly reuse earlier experiments; this is not independent replication of the stability endpoint. Does not refute a stability contribution or establish that all MAT2B effects are stability alone.

targetedChecks.role: Contradictory substrate-order model; contextual to stability
targetedChecks.access: Scite full-text human MAT2A kinetic Results appraised
targetedChecks.assessment: Steady-state, stopped-flow and isotope-exchange evidence supports rapid-equilibrium random substrate binding, conflicting with Bailey's ATP-first model. Retained as a distinct unresolved kinetic issue, not evidence against MAT2B-mediated stability.

retrievalLimited.limitation: Publisher retrieval failed; legitimate Scite full text recovered relevant Results and Methods. Raw immunoblot data and supplementary quantitative half-life reconstruction were not independently reanalysed; Precision remains 1.

record.stoppingRationale: Bounded recovery recovered load-bearing purified-enzyme and cell experiments, screened twelve forward citation edges (truncated discovery, not exhaustive), and examined a conflicting kinetic study and newer structural interpretation. Citation labels/counts were not treated as replication. Further broad retrieval is unlikely to change the model-bounded stability judgement materially.

history.decision: Version 1: proposed experimental Finding, Codex-assessed provisional 5/8; not human-reviewed. Original F1/F4 chemistry and source IDs preserved separately; no canonical admission.

record.title: Dietary protein delivers circulating phenylalanine; kinetics depend on context
record.proposition: Dietary protein supplies phenylalanine to the human circulation, with delivery kinetics varying by the tested protein source, dose and meal context. The pooled age association is context-dependent, not proof that ageing uniformly impairs absorption or that greater availability increases brain neurotransmitters.
record.capRationale: Directness 2, Bias Protection 1 and Precision 1: no D1/B0/P0 ceiling applies. Replication 0 receives no extra decrement.

rationale.D: Direct human dietary tracer appearance tests the specified supply process; concentration-only studies corroborate context, not exact flux.
rationale.B: Controlled isotope methods support supply, but pooled source/dose comparisons are not a single randomised contrast and age is observational. These are appraised residual concerns, not missing evidence automatically scored zero.
rationale.P: Measured appearance is informative, but reported variability and heterogeneous matrices permit materially different magnitudes; no universal age or dosage effect is asserted.
rationale.R: Independent source-response evidence partially corroborates the scoped claim; exact tracer/age/dose comparisons retain research-team dependence. Constituent pooled trials are not counted again.

limitations: Mostly male dairy-tracer cohorts; between-study source/dose contrasts, nonrandomised age comparisons and different matrices limit generalisation. No brain transport, neurotransmitter or ADHD endpoint.

Evidence-confidence conclusions must distinguish limitations of the underlying scientific evidence from limitations of the framework's evidence retrieval and assessment. Absence of verified evidence within an assessment must not be represented as evidence of absence.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: Supporting and null outcomes are endpoint-specific. No uniform age impairment is asserted; exercise and newer source studies qualify that inference.

targetedChecks.access: Full published PDF examined: abstract, data selection, tracer methods, statistics, results and limitations.
targetedChecks.assessment: Pooled 18 laboratory RCT datasets; 602 participants, 590 men; age is not randomised. Dietary tracer enters circulation; protein type and dose affect kinetics. Pooled older-younger difference is not universal age impairment. Five-hour dietary phenylalanine appearance: 50% ± 14% overall; casein 45% ± 11%, whey 57% ± 10%, milk 65% ± 13% (means ± SD). Pooled older/young comparison: 45% ± 10% versus 51% ± 14%; not randomised age assignment. Reported variability and subgroup tests; interstudy comparisons and participant differences limit causal interpretation. One research programme; constituent trials and this pooled analysis must not be counted twice.

targetedChecks.role: supporting; contradicts a universal animal-over-plant hierarchy
targetedChecks.access: Scite full-text Methods and Results, including randomisation, washout, assays, power and multiplicity; published Cambridge PDF checked.
targetedChecks.assessment: Independent Exeter programme; randomised double-blind six-period crossover, 12 young and 10 older adults, both sexes. Source-specific plasma profiles; some non-animal sources produced higher essential-amino-acid responses than the tested milk beverage. Integrated responses did not show a uniform age decrement.  Small cohorts; composition and food matrix differ, so no isolated digestibility estimate or universal ranking follows. Independent of Maastricht pooled dairy corpus; age analyses and six visits within a person are not six independent replications.

targetedChecks.access: Published abstract and full institutional thesis chapter 2 examined.
targetedChecks.assessment: Young/older men, rest/exercise comparisons; 48 participants total. Dietary phenylalanine availability did not differ detectably with exercise although muscle incorporation increased.  Muscle utilisation is not circulating-pool enhancement; a nonsignificant contrast is not equivalence. NCT00557388 is part of Gorissen2020; no double-counting.

previousAssessments.title: Dietary protein delivers circulating phenylalanine; kinetics depend on context
previousAssessments.proposition: Dietary protein supplies phenylalanine to the human circulation, with delivery kinetics varying by the tested protein source, dose and meal context. The pooled age association is context-dependent, not proof that ageing uniformly impairs absorption or that greater availability increases brain neurotransmitters.
previousAssessments.capRationale: Directness 2, Bias Protection 1 and Precision 1: no D1/B0/P0 ceiling applies. Replication 0 receives no extra decrement.

rationale.D: Direct human dietary tracer appearance tests the specified supply process; concentration-only studies corroborate context, not exact flux.
rationale.B: Controlled isotope methods support supply, but pooled source/dose comparisons are not a single randomised contrast and age is observational. These are appraised residual concerns, not missing evidence automatically scored zero.
rationale.P: Measured appearance is informative, but reported variability and heterogeneous matrices permit materially different magnitudes; no universal age or dosage effect is asserted.
rationale.R: Independent source-response evidence partially corroborates the scoped claim; exact tracer/age/dose comparisons retain research-team dependence. Constituent pooled trials are not counted again.

limitations: Mostly male dairy-tracer cohorts; between-study source/dose contrasts, nonrandomised age comparisons and different matrices limit generalisation. No brain transport, neurotransmitter or ADHD endpoint.

targetedChecks.access: Full published PDF examined: abstract, data selection, tracer methods, statistics, results and limitations.
targetedChecks.assessment: Pooled 18 laboratory RCT datasets; 602 participants, 590 men; age is not randomised. Dietary tracer enters circulation; protein type and dose affect kinetics. Pooled older-younger difference is not universal age impairment. Five-hour dietary phenylalanine appearance: 50% ± 14% overall; casein 45% ± 11%, whey 57% ± 10%, milk 65% ± 13% (means ± SD). Pooled older/young comparison: 45% ± 10% versus 51% ± 14%; not randomised age assignment. Reported variability and subgroup tests; interstudy comparisons and participant differences limit causal interpretation. One research programme; constituent trials and this pooled analysis must not be counted twice.

targetedChecks.assessment: Independent Exeter programme; randomised double-blind six-period crossover, 12 young and 10 older adults, both sexes. Source-specific plasma profiles; some non-animal sources produced higher essential-amino-acid responses than the tested milk beverage. Integrated responses did not show a uniform age decrement.  Small cohorts; composition and food matrix differ, so no isolated digestibility estimate or universal ranking follows. Independent of Maastricht pooled dairy corpus; age analyses and six visits within a person are not six independent replications.

targetedChecks.access: Published abstract and full institutional thesis chapter 2 examined.
targetedChecks.assessment: Young/older men, rest/exercise comparisons; 48 participants total. Dietary phenylalanine availability did not differ detectably with exercise although muscle incorporation increased.  Muscle utilisation is not circulating-pool enhancement; a nonsignificant contrast is not equivalence. NCT00557388 is part of Gorissen2020; no double-counting.

record.title: Mincing changed dietary phenylalanine appearance in older men
record.proposition: In a randomised crossover study of ten older men, 135 g minced beef produced greater six-hour dietary phenylalanine appearance than the same quantity of steak. Total plasma essential-amino-acid concentrations and muscle protein synthesis did not differ detectably between preparations.
record.capRationale: Directness 2, Bias Protection 1 and Precision 1: no D1/B0/P0 ceiling applies. Replication 0 receives no extra decrement.

rationale.D: Same-cut beef and isotope-labelled dietary phenylalanine directly test the exact older-men preparation proposition.
rationale.B: Randomised within-person design and matched source/quantity reduce confounding. Visible texture and consumption-time differences remain; concealment and assay masking were not demonstrated in recovered methods. No critical systematic error was established.
rationale.P: Reported tracer effect and standard errors support the directional finding, but n=10, no extracted paired interval and negative secondary outcomes limit magnitude and extrapolation; nulls are not scored as equivalence.
rationale.R: The bounded exact-protocol search and source appraisal yielded one empirical dataset; thesis/journal reports and other processing studies are not independent replications. Independent replication was not established in this assessment.

limitations: One small older-male trial; no independent replication of the exact matched-beef protocol was established in this assessment. No claim that all foods should be minced or that this improves attention.

Evidence-confidence conclusions must distinguish limitations of the underlying scientific evidence from limitations of the framework's evidence retrieval and assessment. Absence of verified evidence within an assessment must not be represented as evidence of absence.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: Supporting and null outcomes are endpoint-specific. No detected total-amino-acid or muscle-synthesis advantage in the same experiment.

targetedChecks.access: Published abstract plus full experimental chapter 6 in the author institutional thesis; final published quantitative result cross-checked against author-shared publication.
targetedChecks.assessment: Randomised crossover; ten older men, mean age 74 years; two visits at least 14 days apart. More dietary phenylalanine appeared after mincing. Total plasma essential-amino-acid concentrations and muscle synthesis did not differ detectably. Six-hour dietary phenylalanine appearance: minced 61% ± 3% versus steak 49% ± 3% (means ± SEM), P < 0.01; 12 percentage-point difference. No paired confidence interval calculated or inferred. Small single trial; mean estimates and standard errors available, paired effect interval not extracted; no equivalence claim for null outcomes. Single empirical dataset; thesis and journal article are the same experiment, not replications.

Total plasma essential-amino-acid concentrations and muscle protein synthesis did not differ detectably between preparations.
record.capRationale: Directness 2, Bias Protection 1 and Precision 1: no D1/B0/P0 ceiling applies. Replication 0 receives no extra decrement.

rationale.D: Same-cut beef and isotope-labelled dietary phenylalanine directly test the exact older-men preparation proposition.
rationale.B: Randomised within-person design and matched source/quantity reduce confounding. Visible texture and consumption-time differences remain; concealment and assay masking were not demonstrated in recovered methods. No critical systematic error was established.
rationale.P: Reported tracer effect and standard errors support the directional finding, but n=10, no extracted paired interval and negative secondary outcomes limit magnitude and extrapolation; nulls are not scored as equivalence.
rationale.R: The bounded exact-protocol search and source appraisal yielded one empirical dataset; thesis/journal reports and other processing studies are not independent replications. Independent replication was not established in this assessment.

limitations: One small older-male trial; no independent replication of the exact matched-beef protocol was established in this assessment. No claim that all foods should be minced or that this improves attention.

Evidence-confidence conclusions must distinguish limitations of the underlying scientific evidence from limitations of the framework's evidence retrieval and assessment. Absence of verified evidence within an assessment must not be represented as evidence of absence.

Intervention disposition: the matched 135 g lean-beef preparation experiment in ten older men remains scientific evidence only. No approved canonical preparation SOP or food-strategy registration is established; exact intervention scope awaits confirmation.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: Supporting and null outcomes are endpoint-specific. No detected total-amino-acid or muscle-synthesis advantage in the same experiment.

targetedChecks.access: Published abstract plus full experimental chapter 6 in the author institutional thesis; final published quantitative result cross-checked against author-shared publication.
targetedChecks.assessment: Randomised crossover; ten older men, mean age 74 years; two visits at least 14 days apart. More dietary phenylalanine appeared after mincing. Total plasma essential-amino-acid concentrations and muscle synthesis did not differ detectably. Six-hour dietary phenylalanine appearance: minced 61% ± 3% versus steak 49% ± 3% (means ± SEM), P < 0.01; 12 percentage-point difference. No paired confidence interval calculated or inferred. Small single trial; mean estimates and standard errors available, paired effect interval not extracted; no equivalence claim for null outcomes. Single empirical dataset; thesis and journal article are the same experiment, not replications.

record.title: Extrusion altered early amino-acid kinetics, not demonstrated total loss
record.proposition: In a randomised crossover of nine healthy young adults, the tested high-moisture-extruded mycoprotein/pea blend delayed selected early plasma amino-acid responses relative to the dry blend. Total five-hour grouped amino-acid availability was not significantly different; the study does not establish poorer overall nutrition for all meat alternatives.
record.capRationale: Directness 2, Bias Protection 1 and Precision 1: no D1/B0/P0 ceiling applies. Replication 0 receives no extra decrement.

rationale.D: The claim is explicitly about measured plasma kinetics in the exact human crossover, not absolute absorption or clinical efficacy.
rationale.B: Randomised counterbalanced double-blind visits and analytical measurement support inference; n=9 and numerous endpoints with residual matrix differences warrant caution, not an invented critical-bias judgement.
rationale.P: Direction of selected early responses is resolved, but null integrated areas lack equivalence bounds; scope excludes a demonstrated total loss.
rationale.R: One matched-product experimental line was assessed. The same group's different protein-source trial and technical in-vitro repeats do not replicate this exact intervention; independent replication was not established in this assessment.

limitations: Single small trial, no dietary tracer, numerous secondary endpoints and laboratory reconstituted products. Not proof of equal total absorption or a reason to avoid all processed plant foods.

Evidence-confidence conclusions must distinguish limitations of the underlying scientific evidence from limitations of the framework's evidence retrieval and assessment. Absence of verified evidence within an assessment must not be represented as evidence of absence.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: Supporting and null outcomes are endpoint-specific. No significant total five-hour grouped exposure difference; not evidence of equivalence.

targetedChecks.role: supporting for kinetic change; null integrated outcomes
targetedChecks.access: Scite full-text human methods, composition, power/statistics and results examined.
targetedChecks.assessment: Randomised double-blind counterbalanced crossover; nine young adults, five men/four women; minimum five-day separation. Extrusion delayed early responses and reduced selected peaks, including phenylalanine and tyrosine. Total five-hour grouped amino-acid availability was not significantly different. Phenylalanine peak: dry blend 72 ± 3 versus extruded 58 ± 3 micromol/L, P=0.020; time to peak 32 ± 4 versus 83 ± 20 minutes, P=0.037 (means ± SEM). Total five-hour grouped amino-acid iAUC: no statistically significant difference; no equivalence bounds inferred. Small single dataset; no tracer, many endpoints, uncertainty on paired differences; laboratory reconstituted products not every commercial meat alternative. Distinct study but same Exeter programme as nonanimal2024; not an independent replication of its six-source comparison.

record.capRationale: D2: no inferential cap for the plasma proposition. No B0/P0 cap applies. R1 limits replication credit; no extra deduction.

rationale.D: 2/2: controlled feeding studies measure the scoped plasma ratio directly. Human brain uptake and benefit are explicitly excluded.
rationale.B: 1/2: Wurtman randomised meal order, used objective assays and order-adjusted/multiplicity-aware analysis. Visible meals, one incomplete participant and incompletely established protections in historical and protein-source studies leave residual concerns; no critical bias is demonstrated.
rationale.P: 1/2: source-specific contrasts and reported SEM/ranges distinguish a meal effect in tested conditions. Small samples, heterogeneous protocols and limited paired uncertainty leave materially different magnitudes and boundaries plausible. Null experiments are not equivalence results.
rationale.R: 1/2: separate investigator groups and datasets corroborate plasma meal responsiveness, but protocol/denominator differences and credible evening/starch nulls preclude full replication credit. This is not independent replication of one exact meal protocol.

limitations: Small acute healthy-adult samples; different meals, ratio denominators and sampling windows; incomplete historical methods retrieval. No population-wide optimum or direct human brain-flux estimate. Evening null results limit generalisation but are not equivalence evidence.

record.title: Mitochondrial oxidant production is source- and state-dependent
record.proposition: Specific mitochondrial electron-transfer sites generate superoxide and hydrogen peroxide; source-specific suppression can reduce oxidant production without inhibiting oxidative phosphorylation. Succinate oxidation during reperfusion can drive excessive production through reverse electron transport.
record.process: Codex bounded PM4/PM5 SEC completion v1: exact propositions, primary full-text recovery, factor-specific appraisal, scoped independence and explicit unresolved judgements; no human scientific-review status inferred.

methodology.name: Existing SEC four-factor anchors and integrated caps

rationale.D: Brand site-selective suppressors and Chouchani reperfusion perturbations test source generation, respiration and reverse-electron-transport endpoints in the stated experimental models (Brand Figs 1–2, 5; Chouchani Figs 2–4). No food or human efficacy proposition is scored.
rationale.B: Source counterscreens and respiration controls limit nonspecific inhibition, and reperfusion experiments add tracer/pharmacological checks. Tool selectivity and between-model transfer remain material residual concerns; this is not a fully bias-protected dietary trial.
rationale.P: Dose-response/selectivity and respiratory measurements discriminate source suppression from generalized inhibition. The limits of selectivity and translation across preparations leave uncertainty in effect size and applicable source boundaries; P2 is not established.
rationale.R: The two research programmes provide partially matching evidence for source-dependent complex-I oxidant regulation. They do not independently replicate every component of this composite Finding; multiple models within Brand are not counted as independent research-group replication.

record.capRationale: No D1/B0/P0 ceiling applies; adjusted equals raw. No extra model-to-human penalty is added because the proposition remains model-specific.
limitations: Experimental suppressors and ischaemia models establish source regulation, not dietary effectiveness. These results do not imply that all mitochondrial ROS are harmful or that mitochondrial emission assays isolate gross production.

methodology.name: Existing SEC four-factor anchors and integrated caps

rationale.D: Anderson Fig. 6 tests the specified meal/short-feeding exposure and human muscle H2O2 emission. Its separate rodent interventions support the separately stated rodent clause, not human mediation.
rationale.B: Within-person baseline and validated emission/respirometry assays help attribution, but the sequential human feeding design lacks a randomized contemporaneous meal comparator; diet/time/order confounding remains. The scored statement is the observed experiment, not a causal replacement-diet claim.

rationale.R: Only one independent human feeding dataset supports the exact meal/five-day muscle-emission result in the bounded assessed body. The obese cross-section and rodent arms do not replicate that exposure/population proposition. R0 describes this scoped body, not proof of absence throughout the literature.

rationale.D: Gram measures H2O2 emission at controlled membrane potential before immobilisation and after retraining; Fig. 9 directly matches the principal claim. The separate acute study supplies only the distinct respiratory-state-dependent clause.

rationale.B: Isoform-specific knockout/control comparisons, lipid assays and dietary rescue improve attribution. Small tissue/model samples, developmental effects and incomplete protection against allocation/litter-related confounding remain; tissue divergence is retained.

record.title: Mitochondrial glutathione requires compartmental transport
record.proposition: SLC25A39 perturbation and organelle uptake experiments establish that mitochondrial glutathione depends on import. Precursor supply, cytosolic synthesis, mitochondrial transport and local glutathione use are separate steps.
record.process: Codex bounded PM4/PM5 SEC completion v1: exact propositions, primary full-text recovery, factor-specific appraisal, scoped independence and explicit unresolved judgements; no human scientific-review status inferred.

methodology.name: Existing SEC four-factor anchors and integrated caps

rationale.D: Wang and Shi directly measure mitochondrial GSH and isotope-labelled organelle uptake after SLC25A39 perturbation. The scored proposition is compartmental import, not GSH antioxidant efficacy, dietary precursor success or clinical protection.
rationale.B: Independent genetic perturbations, cDNA rescue, tag/background controls, organelle separation, isotope uptake time courses and structure-function mutants address off-target, contamination and indirect synthesis explanations (Wang Fig. 3; Shi Figs 4–5). These are design-appropriate protections for this biochemical proposition.
rationale.P: Uptake contrasts, time courses and rescue/mutant comparisons with independent biological samples and LC-MS quality controls resolve the qualitative presence of an import dependency. The decision boundary is discrimination from intact uptake after knockout or merely cytosolic depletion; no precise human flux is inferred.
rationale.R: Wang (Birsoy group) and Shi (Shen group) independently establish the same SLC25A39/GSH-import relationship with distinct screens and uptake experiments. Colell is context for transport limitations, not a third SLC25A39 replication.

record.capRationale: No D1/B0/P0 ceiling applies; adjusted equals raw. No extra model-to-human penalty is added because the proposition remains model-specific.
limitations: Glutathione-dependent iron–sulfur-cluster maintenance is not interchangeable with peroxide detoxification. Cytosolic or blood glutathione does not establish mitochondrial delivery; in ethanol-fed rats NAC failed to restore mitochondrial GSH whereas SAM supplementation did.
